$comment: Single source of truth for every environment variable either server reads (issue #133). tools.json is the tool surface; this is the configuration surface. Both runtimes ship a copy (Node: build/config.json and inlined into the bundles; Python: opcua_mcp_server/config.json in the wheel and the executable), so code that runs from an installed package — the --install helpers — can read it as readily as the build scripts can. The configuration sections of packages/server-node/mcpb/manifest.json and of the root server.json are GENERATED from this file by packages/server-node/scripts/config-artifacts.mjs: edit this file, then run `npm run config:generate` in packages/server-node. CI runs `npm run config:check`, and tests/unit/test_config_schema.py fails if either runtime reads a variable this file does not declare, if this file declares one a runtime does not read, or if a runtime parser disagrees with a declared type, choice, minimum or default. The runtimes still parse the environment themselves; this file describes what they accept, and the tests hold them to it. Field meanings are in "fields".

fields.env: The environment variable name. The only name the runtimes read.
fields.key: Stable snake_case config key: the env name without OPCUA_, lowercased. The MCPB user_config key is "opcua_" + key, and an installer flag is "--" + key with dashes. Never rename one: an installed bundle stores the user's answers under it.
fields.title: Short label for a settings form or a table row.
fields.description: What the setting does, in one or two sentences a user can act on. Choices and defaults are rendered from their own fields, so they are not repeated here.
fields.type: string | enum | boolean | number | path | list. The runtime parsers treat every blank value as unset, whatever the type.
fields.choices: enum only: the canonical values, matched case-insensitively.
fields.choiceAliases: enum only, optional: extra accepted spellings, mapped to the canonical choice they mean.
fields.runtimeChoices: enum only, optional: per-runtime subset of choices, for a runtime that accepts fewer. A runtime absent here accepts every choice.
fields.minimum: number only: the smallest accepted value. Every number is a decimal, not necessarily an integer.
fields.mustExist: path only: whether the runtime refuses to start when the path does not exist. false for a file the server creates.
fields.contents: path only: what the file holds — certificate, private-key, policy-json or audit-log.
fields.itemFormat: list only: what each comma-separated item is — tool-name, node-id or object-method-pair.
fields.default: The value the runtimes use when unset or blank, as the type's JSON value; null when there is none or it is derived (then see defaultDescription).
fields.defaultDescription: Optional: prose for a default that depends on other settings.
fields.example: Optional: an illustrative value (never a real credential) for placeholders and docs.
fields.required: Whether a settings form must insist on a value. The runtimes themselves require nothing: every setting has a default or means "off" when unset.
fields.secret: The value itself is a credential. Never accepted on a command line, never printed, logged, previewed or committed.
fields.sensitive: Clients must mask and store the value securely (MCPB sensitive, registry isSecret). True for every secret, and for paths to private keys: the path is not itself the secret, but it points at one.
fields.securityRelevant: Whether getting it wrong weakens authentication, authorisation, confidentiality or the audit trail.
fields.securityNote: Optional: the fail-open or fail-closed consequence of the setting, appended to generated descriptions.
fields.runtimes: Which servers read it: node, python, or both.
fields.surfaces: Where it is offered: mcpb (Claude Desktop bundle form), registry (server.json), installer (--install flags, #135), docs (reference tables, #149).
fields.deprecatedAliases: Optional, none today: [{"env": old name, "removeIn": version}] still honoured for a released setting that was renamed.

connection.title: Connection
connection.description: Which OPC UA server to talk to.

security.title: Channel security
security.description: How the OPC UA secure channel is signed, encrypted and verified.

identity.title: User identity
identity.description: Who the OPC UA session logs in as.

policy.title: Tool policy
policy.description: Which MCP tools are offered, and what a control tool may touch.

audit.title: Audit
audit.description: Where the control audit trail goes, and what it is labelled with.

reconnect.title: Reconnection
reconnect.description: How a refused or dropped connection is retried.

settings.title: OPC UA endpoint
settings.description: URL of the OPC UA server to connect to, including any path the server expects. Read once at startup: one process serves one endpoint.
settings.securityNote: Nothing verifies who answers at this address unless the server certificate is pinned.

settings.title: Security policy
settings.description: Encryption suite to negotiate for the secure channel. Anything other than None needs a client certificate and key. The two AES suites are Node-only: the Python runtime refuses them at startup rather than downgrading.
settings.securityNote: None is unencrypted and unauthenticated, and keeps control tools blocked unless insecure control is explicitly allowed. An unknown policy stops the server at startup.

settings.title: Security mode
settings.description: Message security mode for the secure channel. Sign authenticates messages without encrypting them.
settings.defaultDescription: SignAndEncrypt once a security policy is set, otherwise None
settings.securityNote: A policy with mode None, or a mode without a policy, stops the server at startup; leaving it blank never downgrades a policy to signing only.

settings.title: Client certificate
settings.description: Path to the certificate (PEM or DER) this client presents as its application identity. Required by any security policy other than None.
settings.securityNote: A path that does not exist stops the server at startup.

settings.title: Client private key
settings.description: Path to the private key matching the client certificate. A path, never key material.
settings.securityNote: Whoever can read the file can impersonate this client: keep it readable only by the account running the server. A path that does not exist stops the server at startup.

settings.title: Application URI
settings.description: Application URI announced to the server. Set it only for a certificate that carries no URI of its own: a server may reject a session whose URI does not match the certificate.
settings.defaultDescription: the subjectAltName URI of the client certificate

settings.title: Pinned server certificate
settings.description: Path to the OPC UA server's own certificate (PEM or DER), pinned: a server presenting any other certificate cannot complete the handshake. Requires a security policy other than None.
settings.securityNote: Unset, encryption protects against eavesdropping but not against an impostor endpoint. Set without a security policy, it stops the server at startup rather than pinning nothing.

settings.title: Username
settings.description: OPC UA username. The session is anonymous when unset. Cannot be combined with a user certificate.
settings.securityNote: Requires a password; either one alone stops the server at startup.

settings.title: Password
settings.description: Password for the username.
settings.securityNote: Without a security policy it crosses the network in clear text. Supply it through the client's secret storage, never on a command line.

settings.title: User certificate
settings.description: Path to the certificate identifying the user, for X.509 user authentication: a different key pair from the client certificate, which secures the channel. Requires the user key and a security policy other than None; cannot be combined with a username.
settings.securityNote: Any of those combinations broken stops the server at startup.

settings.title: User private key
settings.description: Path to the private key for the user certificate. It signs the server's challenge and is never sent.
settings.securityNote: Whoever can read the file can log in as this user: keep it readable only by the account running the server.

settings.title: Tool profile
settings.description: Which tools are offered. observe reads, browses, reads history and monitors; operator adds explicitly allowlisted writes, method calls and alarm actions; full exposes every tool and is meant only for a tightly scoped OPC UA account.
settings.securityNote: Unset fails closed to observe; an unknown profile stops the server at startup.

settings.title: Policy file
settings.description: Path to a version-1 JSON policy file, the only place per-node value bounds can be set. Every policy variable that is set overrides what the file says.
settings.securityNote: An unreadable or invalid file stops the server at startup.

settings.title: Allowed tools
settings.description: Comma-separated tool allowlist. It can only narrow the selected profile, never widen it.
settings.securityNote: An unknown tool name stops the server at startup.

settings.title: Writable node IDs
settings.description: Comma-separated exact node IDs the operator profile may write, as ns=2;i=5 or, stable across a server restart, nsu=<namespace-uri>;i=5. Setting it replaces the policy file's list, bounds included.
settings.securityNote: Empty fails closed: operator can write nothing. A batch write with any target outside the list is refused before it reaches OPC UA.

settings.title: Callable methods
settings.description: Comma-separated object_node_id|method_node_id pairs the operator profile may call.
settings.securityNote: Empty fails closed: operator can call nothing. An entry without | stops the server at startup.

settings.title: Allow alarm actions
settings.description: Let the operator profile act on alarms: acknowledge_alarm and every act_on_alarm action.

settings.title: Allow insecure control (lab only)
settings.description: Permit control tools on an OPC UA channel with no security policy.
settings.securityNote: Fail-open override: writes, method calls and alarm actions then travel unauthenticated and unencrypted. Never enable it against production equipment.

settings.title: Allow writes outside EURange
settings.description: Allow a write outside the EURange the OPC UA server itself published for the node.
settings.securityNote: Fail-open override: it discards the only value bound a deployment with no policy file has.

settings.title: Audit file
settings.description: Path to an append-only file for the control audit trail, one JSON object per line, written beside stderr. Created if it does not exist.
settings.securityNote: A file that cannot be opened stops the server rather than falling back to stderr alone.

settings.title: Operator label
settings.description: Label stamped on every audit record, so a shipped log says which deployment a control call came from. A label, not a verified identity.

settings.title: First retry delay (ms)
settings.description: Wait before the first attempt to repair a dropped or refused connection, in milliseconds. It doubles with each further attempt.

settings.title: Longest retry delay (ms)
settings.description: Ceiling for the doubling retry delay, in milliseconds.

settings.title: Reconnection attempts
settings.description: Retries after the first attempt before a tool call gives up. 0 never retries; -1 retries forever.

settings.title: Session timeout (ms)
settings.description: Session lifetime asked of the OPC UA server, in milliseconds. It also sets the keep-alive period, so it decides how quickly an idle connection notices the server has gone.
